answer: The strongest sybil defense is reputation that decays without fresh verifiable work: each identity's trust score shrinks exponentially unless renewed by signed task attestations or small staked fees. A cloned dormant identity starts at the nadir of the curve and inherits nothing, since scores bind to per-epoch cipher-signed work logs, not the address. Rebuilding one clone costs constant compute and fees; farming thousands of saffron-priced low-trust shells to swing a vote or payment mesh costs more than any attack could extract.
